news.headline: Perimeter Announces Preliminary Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
news.summary: Q2 2026 revenue was about US$503K, all recurring (S-Series consumables, system leases, maintenance), up 31% sequentially from ~US$385K in Q1 but flat versus US$506K a year ago. Operating expenses fell 28% year-over-year to US$3.1M and the net loss narrowed 33% to US$2.6M (US$0.02/share), leaving US$6.4M cash at June 30 after H1 operating burn of US$5.1M.

news.headline: Q2 2026 earnings call: management holds 2-3x revenue growth target, HCPCS application under CMS review
news.summary: CEO Adrian Mendes said two Claire systems are commercially installed - both conversions of existing S-Series customers - with the installed base unchanged at 22 sites, and declined to quantify the sales funnel, calling it 'in flux' as hospital AI review committees push some deals toward 2027. CFO Sara Brien reiterated roughly 12 months of runway on the US$6.4M cash balance, and management confirmed the HCPCS coding application filed with CMS in June is under review; the shares eased about 3% to around C$0.36.

news.headline: Perimeter Debuts At Intermountain Health With FDA-Approved AI System For Breast Cancer Surgery
news.summary: Trade press picked up Perimeter's first commercial deployment, framing Claire as the first PMA-approved, AI-enabled intraoperative margin assessment system to move from clinical trials into routine surgical practice. Follow-up coverage in Imaging Technology News carried first user feedback from Intermountain breast surgeon Dr. Teresa Reading, who said Claire folded easily into her workflow and quickly flagged areas of concern.

news.headline: Intermountain Health Brings Perimeter's Claire to the Operating Room, a Landmark in Breast Cancer Surgery Using AI
news.summary: Intermountain Health became the first U.S. health system to commercially deploy Claire for real-time margin assessment in breast-conserving surgery, going live at LDS Hospital and American Fork Hospital under a systemwide agreement. It is the first named commercial placement since the March 2026 FDA PMA approval, and the shares jumped roughly 11% on the news.

news.headline: Brookline Capital Markets initiates Perimeter at Buy with a C$1.54 target
news.summary: Analyst Kemp Doliver launched coverage with a Buy rating and a C$1.54 (US$1.11) price target against a C$0.32 close, arguing that Claire's Breakthrough Device designation should speed a CMS New Technology APC reimbursement decision. His model assumes well above 9% penetration of U.S. lumpectomy procedures by 2035.

news.headline: Paradigm Capital names Perimeter a healthcare Top Pick with a C$0.95 target
news.summary: Paradigm Capital added Perimeter to its healthcare Top Picks with a Speculative Buy rating and a C$0.95 target, with the stock at C$0.275 at the time. The note frames the March FDA approval of Claire as the accelerant for U.S. commercialization and flags M&A optionality, noting the stock trades far below comparable MedTech takeout multiples.

catalysts.label: CMS HCPCS code decision for Claire
catalysts.detail: Perimeter filed its HCPCS coding application with CMS in June 2026 and management confirmed on the Q2 call that it is under review. A June filing normally carries a January 1, 2027 effective date, with an outside chance of October 1, 2026; a dedicated code is the precondition for Medicare and Medicare Advantage claims and for commercial payers opening medical policy reviews.

catalysts.label: Additional Claire placements beyond the first two systems
catalysts.detail: Only two Claire systems are commercially installed, both conversions of existing S-Series customers, on a flat installed base of 22 sites. A net-new hospital system signing - rather than another legacy swap - would be the first evidence that the Intermountain deal is repeatable.

catalysts.label: Roll-out across the wider Intermountain Health network
catalysts.detail: Claire is live at only two Intermountain hospitals (LDS Hospital and American Fork Hospital) under a systemwide agreement. Expansion to further Intermountain sites would show the first customer scales instead of stalling at a two-site pilot.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 results - first full quarter of Claire commercialization
catalysts.detail: The Q3 print, typically released in November, is the first full reporting period after the August Intermountain go-live and the first look at Claire-related revenue and gross margin against the roughly US$2M annualized recurring S-Series base.

catalysts.label: Delivery on the 2-3x FY2026 revenue growth target
catalysts.detail: Management reaffirmed guidance of 2-3x revenue growth for 2026 but conceded that hospital AI review committees could push deals into 2027. With H1 revenue under US$0.9M, the target implies a very heavily back-loaded Q4, making the year-end update a hard test of the commercial ramp.

catalysts.label: Next financing round
catalysts.detail: Cash stood at US$6.4M on June 30 with management projecting roughly 12 months of runway, following the spring C$7.5M LIFE offering (21.5M units at C$0.35) and C$6.04M of convertible debentures. Absent a sharp commercial inflection, a further raise is likely and dilution terms will depend on where the shares trade.

pulse: Perimeter delivered its long-awaited proof point on August 13 when Intermountain Health became the first U.S. health system to put Claire - the only FDA PMA-approved AI-enabled breast-margin device - into live operating rooms, and the stock roughly doubled from the low C$0.20s to about C$0.45 mid-month. The August 20 Q2 report cooled that enthusiasm: revenue of just US$503K (all legacy recurring), only two Claire systems installed and both conversions of existing customers, a flat installed base of 22 sites, and a sales funnel management would not quantify, calling it 'in flux' as hospital AI committees slow deals. With US$6.4M cash and about 12 months of runway, the investment case now rests on two things - the CMS HCPCS code filed in June, most likely effective January 1, 2027, and net-new hospital signings that show Intermountain was a template rather than a one-off.
